Description: Core Lost and Found full-stack application modules for campus community
Acceptance Criteria: All user-facing CRUD modules, search filtering, and rule-based matching engine implemented and functional.

Description: Complete CI/CD, Containerization, Provisioning and Orchestration pipeline for Experiments 1 through 7
Acceptance Criteria: All syllabus DevOps experiments integrated into one cohesive automated delivery workflow.

Description: As a college student who lost an item, I want to submit a detailed report so that anyone who finds it can return it.
Acceptance Criteria: Form accepts title, category, description, location, date, optional image, contact info (name, email, phone). Creates item with type=LOST, status=ACTIVE.

Description: As a finder of a lost item, I want to submit a report with item details and location so the rightful owner can locate it.
Acceptance Criteria: Form accepts identical fields with type=FOUND, status=ACTIVE. Validates email and phone. Returns 201 Created.

Description: As a user, I want to search reported items with keyword search and category/location/type filters so I can quickly identify items.
Acceptance Criteria: Search bar searches title and description. Dropdown filters for category, location, and type (LOST/FOUND). Fast responsive card display.

Summary: View Item Details and Contact Info
Description: As a user, I want to view the complete details of an item along with safe contact details to verify ownership.
Acceptance Criteria: Dedicated item detail view showing full metadata, reporter contact card, report date, and status badge.

Description: Configure Git repository, base branches (main, develop), feature branch conventions, PR template, and commit conventions.
Acceptance Criteria: Repo initialized with .gitignore, README.md, develop and feature branches, PR template, and Conventional Commit standard enforced.

Description: As a user, I want the system to automatically compare newly reported items against opposite items and display a 'Possible Match' banner when score > 60%.
Acceptance Criteria: Matching engine scores: Category 30%, Title 30%, Location 25%, Description 15%. If score > 60%, match record created and 'Possible Match' banner rendered.

Summary: Continuous Integration Pipeline with GitHub Actions
Description: Implement GitHub Actions workflow to run linting, unit/API tests against a PostgreSQL container, build frontend, and verify Docker builds on push/PR.
Acceptance Criteria: ci.yml executes on push/PR to main/develop. Passing checks gate pull requests. Status badge embedded in README.

Description: Build secure, lightweight multi-stage Dockerfiles for backend and frontend with non-root user and healthchecks.
Acceptance Criteria: Multi-stage builds using node:20-alpine. Non-root user node. Built-in HEALTHCHECK on both images.

Description: Configure docker-compose.yml for frontend, backend, and postgres services with isolated networks, persistent volumes, and health-dependent startup.
Acceptance Criteria: docker-compose.yml brings up 3 services. Uses condition: service_healthy for ordered startup. Database data persists across restarts.

Summary: Host Provisioning and Configuration with Ansible
Description: Create Ansible playbooks and roles to configure Docker, dependencies, application deployment directory, and launch containers idempotently.
Acceptance Criteria: roles/docker and roles/app created. Playbook passes syntax check. Second run returns changed=0 proving idempotence.

Description: Deploy PostgreSQL with PVC, Backend with 2 replicas and health probes, and Frontend on Kubernetes with ConfigMaps and Secrets.
Acceptance Criteria: Standard K8s manifests in k8s/. Backend runs 2 replicas with liveness and readiness probes on /health. PersistentVolumeClaim bound for DB.

Description: Expose services via ClusterIP and NodePort, verify horizontal scaling to 3 replicas, zero-downtime rolling updates, and self-healing pod recovery.
Acceptance Criteria: kubectl scale scales backend to 3 replicas. Deleting a pod triggers instant self-healing. Rolling update and undo demonstrated.
